Absence of a flag is not a guarantee of safety, presence of a flag is not an accusation of wrongdoing, and no part of this report is financial advice. Nobody pays KAY9 for an audit: access is a refundable lock of KAY9 and nothing a requester does or declares can change a score. notes: A category is scored internally as accumulated risk -- the sum of each signal in that category, weighted by its own confidence, clamped to 0..100 -- and published as trust, 100 minus that accumulation, so a higher published number always means more trustworthy.
Signals are summed in ascending code order so the result does not depend on the order data arrived in.
A category whose data could not be gathered is held at or below a published trust ceiling of 65 and raises INSUFFICIENT_DATA; missing data never raises a trust score.

The published overall trust score is 100 minus the weighted mean of the risk accumulations of the categories this scan actually measured, renormalized to their own combined weight -- a category held at the uncertainty floor does not otherwise pull the headline number toward it -- then held at or below 40 if any scoring signal is high severity and at or below 20 if any is critical. If nothing could be measured, overall sits at the same uncertainty ceiling as any other unmeasured category.

`measuredWeight` (0..1, alongside `confidence`) is the share of the category weight that fed the overall score; a reader should trust a headline number in proportion to it, since a low risk built on a small measured slice is not the same claim as a low risk built on all seven.
Scores are trust, not a quality rating: 100 means nothing risky was observed, 0 means the worst observable state. They are never a recommendation.

Scores from the probabilistic layer -- wallet clustering, Sybil and insider grouping, wash-trading likelihood and creator fingerprinting -- are snapped to the nearest 5 before they are scored, so that independent implementations of those heuristics can agree on a value without coordinating on one. Every signal marked probabilistic in this report was rounded that way; the deterministic core was not.
Categories scored at the uncertainty floor in this run: bot, creator, holder, insider, liquidity, trading.
methodology.scoring: Each signal contributes points to one risk category internally, weighted by its own confidence; category risk is combined into an overall risk with fixed weights and published as trust, 100 minus that risk. See docs/AUDIT_PROTOCOL.md for the full table.

weights.description: Powers the deployed code grants: minting, pausing, deny-lists, mutable fees, upgradeability, privileged balance movement, and whether source is verified.
Depth of the discovered pools on the quote side, and whether the provider position is locked or burned.
Concentration of circulating supply across the sampled holders, with pools, burn addresses and the token contract itself excluded.
Wallets that share a funding source, and transfers that fund several recipients at once.
The deployer address and the deployment pattern visible in its sampled history.
Round-trip transfer patterns between the same addresses, and whether the token trades at all.
How much of the earliest distribution a small set of addresses captured.

signals.detail: Locating a deployment means asking what the chain looked like in the past, which needs an archive node, and enumerating a deployer’s other launches needs an address-indexed transaction history that standard JSON-RPC does not expose. Neither is available to a scan running in a browser against a public endpoint, so no conclusion is drawn about this deployer in either direction.
signals.title: Deployer and deployer history not scanned at this tier

signals.detail: The Transfer log was read up to block 629999 without finding the first transfer, so the early-buyer window could not be positioned. Sniper and bundling heuristics were not evaluated.
signals.title: Early-buyer window not read

signals.detail: Holder concentration is reconstructed by folding every Transfer log into balances, and the log range could not be read in full. A partial fold is not reported, because a holder whose only incoming transfer fell outside the range would disappear and make the remaining holders look larger than they are. The absence of a concentration flag here means nothing was measured, not that the distribution is healthy.
signals.title: Holder distribution unavailable

signals.detail: The pools found hold less than this chain’s threshold, but the blocks searched do not cover the whole life of this token, so a pool created earlier would not have been seen — and a launchpad’s graduation pool is usually the oldest. The depth that was read is not compared with the threshold.

signals.detail: Uniswap v3 and v4 positions are NFTs, so whether they are locked depends on who owns each position token. The pool search did not reach back to this token’s first block, so the positions in an older pool were not read, and a conclusion about the pools found is not a conclusion about its liquidity.
signals.title: Liquidity lock state not determinable
